title: Vanishing in the universal curve test
statement:
Let $X\to S$ be affine smooth of relative dimension one with $X$
affine, $S=\Spec A$ with $A$ a normal domain with algebraically closed
fraction field $L$, $K/L$ an extension of algebraically closed fields
with $g$ the corresponding geometric generic point of $S$, $d$ an integer
invertible on $S$, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y=X\times_S\Spec K\\
f\downarrow & & \downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;g\;} & \Spec K.
\end{array}
$$

Then

$$
R^qh_*(\Lambda/d\Lambda)=0\qquad(q\ge1)
$$

for the constant sheaf $\Lambda/d\Lambda$ on $Y_{\Et}$.

proof.text: Put $n=|d|$. Since $A$ is a nonzero domain and $d$ is invertible in $A$, $d\ne0$, hence $n\ge1$. The ideals $d\Lambda$ and $n\Lambda$ agree, since $d=\pm n$, and $n$ is invertible on $S$. Fix a positive cohomological degree $q$, regarded as a natural number. These replacements do not change the coefficient sheaf or the desired conclusion.

source.place: Reduction to cyclic coefficients; explicit normalization of the signed integer d

proof.text: The map $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a morphism between affine schemes and therefore affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. In the displayed Cartesian square, $h:Y\to X$ is the base change of $g$ along $f$ (not the base change of $f$). Clauses (1) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] make $h$ affine and then quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These are precisely the geometric hypotheses needed for coefficient reduction.

source.place: 01SH, lemma-morphism-affines-affine; 01SD, lemma-base-change-affine; 01S7, lemma-affine-separated. Corrects the side named in the blueprint reduction paragraph.

proof.text: Let $e$ be any natural-number divisor of $n$. Then $e\ge1$, and writing $n=ea$ shows that $e$ is invertible on $S$: an inverse is $a n^{-1}$. Apply [sbc-thm-universal-test-vanishing] to the same square and integer $e$. Its hypotheses are exactly those already assumed here: $X\to S$ is affine smooth of relative dimension one with $X$ affine; $A$ is a normal domain with algebraically closed fraction field $L$; $K/L$ is an algebraically closed extension; and $g$ is the specified geometric generic map, induced by $A\subset L\subset K$. It yields $R^q h_*\underline{\mathbf Z/e\mathbf Z}=0$ as an abelian sheaf for every $e\mid n$. This existing split in the same unit carries the sheafified-presheaf argument, affine-curve vanishing for $q>1$, and the slicing, invariance, torsor-component and spreading argument for $q=1$; none of those steps is replaced.

source.place: The cyclic case: sheafified cohomology presheaf paragraph and both degree bullets, already realized by sbc-thm-universal-test-vanishing

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-constant-module-higher-direct-image-cyclic-reduction] to $h$, the arbitrary commutative ring $\Lambda$, and the natural numbers $n,q$. Step 2 gives its quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses; step 3 supplies its vanishing hypothesis for every divisor of $n$. Its conclusion is exactly $R^q h_*\underline{\Lambda/n\Lambda}=0$ in sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules. By step 1 this is $R^q h_*\underline{\Lambda/d\Lambda}=0$. Since $q\ge1$ was arbitrary, all the asserted higher direct images vanish. No finiteness hypothesis on $\Lambda$ is imposed by the cited reduction.

lean.note: Exact existing source declaration, read from the current WeilConjectures source with scompile.py --source. It states the arbitrary-commutative-ring vanishing on a CurveTestDatum: the datum fields encode an affine integral normal base with algebraically closed function field, an affine smooth relative-dimension-one curve and its specified geometric-generic Cartesian fibre, and a natural torsion order invertible on the base. The theorem quantifies q : ℤ with 1 ≤ q and concludes IsZero of Etale.higherDirectImage in sheaves of Λ-modules. The node uses an integer d; the source declaration uses d.natAbs, which gives the same quotient because (d)=(|d|), including negative d and d=0 excluded by invertibility. The bundle’s affine integral normal base is equivalent to Spec of a normal domain, and affine f over an affine base implies affine X, so no source hypothesis is lost. No new module is needed.
lean.statement:
theorem Etale.CurveTestDatum.isZero_higherDirectImage_constantSheaf
    (D : Etale.CurveTestDatum.{u}) (q : ℤ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    IsZero (Etale.higherDirectImage Λ D.h q (Etale.constantModSheaf Λ D.Y₀ D.d))
